name: Spanish Arroz Meloso de Rape y Gambas

components.name: Arroz Meloso with Monkfish and Prawns
steps: Cut monkfish into bite-size pieces. Use 450 g peeled prawns, reserving shells for stock only if supplied separately.
Heat 35 ml olive oil in a broad shallow pot and sear monkfish and prawns very briefly, then lift to a plate.
Cook 110 g grated onion and 180 g tomato in the same pot until the sofrito thickens. Stir in paprika and saffron.
Mix in the 35 g almond-based picada, 10 g garlic and 15 g parsley, then add 320 g rice and coat in sofrito.
Add roughly 1200 ml hot stock; stir frequently and simmer, adding more up to 1400 ml if needed, until rice becomes creamy and just tender.
Return monkfish and prawns only for final minutes to cook thoroughly. Finish with lemon; serve immediately rather than freezing.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

Benicàssim source includes 250 g monkfish, 12 prawns, 200 g rice and 1200 g stock, but does not state a base serving number. UNHANGRY scales the core dish to 4 substantial servings using original technique; quantities are an adaptation.

Storing & reheating: Meloso rice must be served soon after cooking for the intended texture; refrigeration causes thickening. Prepare seafood stock and sofrito in advance; cook rice closer to serving.
Allergens: Fish, Shellfish / molluscs, Tree nuts

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Best on cooking day — cook the rice close to serving.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
